# Erdős Problem 487

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/487](https://www.erdosproblems.com/487)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [DaEr36] Davenport, H. and Erdős, P., *On sequences of positive integers*. Acta Arithmetica
  (1936), 147-151.
- [Kl71] Kleitman, Daniel, *Collections of subsets containing no two sets and their union*.
  Proceedings of the LA Meeting AMS (1971), 153-155.

namespace Erdos487

/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ have positive density. Must there exist distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such
that $[a,b]=c$ (where $[a,b]$ is the least common multiple of $a$ and $b$)?

This is true, a consequence of the positive solution to [447] by Kleitman [Kl71].

Davenport and Erdős [DaEr36] showed that there must exist an infinite sequence $a_1<a_2\cdots$
in $A$ such that $a_i\mid a_j$ for all $i\leq j$, under the assumption that the upper logarithmic
density of $A$ is positive.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos487.lean"]
theorem erdos_487 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.HasPosDensity →
      ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ b ≠ c ∧ a ≠ c ∧ Nat.lcm a b = c := by
  sorry

end Erdos487

reformulations.difference: The conclusion requires one distinct LCM triple. Er61, §II.1, p. 239, and the related problem-447 remark also give an infinitely-many-triples formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the same positive natural-density hypothesis, the universally quantified one-triple assertion is equivalent to requiring infinitely many triples in every such set. Finite deletion preserves positive density. If a set had only finitely many triples, delete their first coordinates. Applying the universal one-triple assertion to the remaining positive-density subset produces a triple in the original set whose first coordinate was deleted, a contradiction. Conversely, an infinite set of triples is nonempty. The scratch theorem one_triple_iff_infinitely_many proves this equivalence without using the sorry-backed problem theorem.

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully matches problem 487 and Er61, p. 236. The source explicitly defines density as an existing natural-density limit. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved equivalence of the repository's [0,N) counting convention with the source's [1,N] convention, excluded finite/empty sets from the hypothesis, tested small LCM triples, and proved that distinct LCM triples cannot involve zero. The density and infinitude equivalence proofs compile with only standard axioms. The current source records an affirmative solution verified in Lean, agreeing with all metadata. The pinned external proof has a stronger positive-lower-density hypothesis; a scratch proof verifies that the file's hypothesis implies it. Both linked proof files were inspected for placeholders/custom axioms, but their Lean 4.29.1 project was not rebuilt under the supplied Lean 4.33.1 environment. Kleitman's full chapter was inaccessible behind publisher login; its bibliographic record and the relevant accessible Erdős passages were checked. No repository files were changed.
